newsitem.title: SWEDEN: POLL - Swedish PM's popularity plunges.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Swedish PM's popularity plunges.

text.p: Only 17 percent of Swedes want to see Prime Minister Goran Persson in place after next year's general election, while 40 percent prefer Bosnian peacemaker Carl Bildt, an opinion poll showed on Sunday.

Persson, under fire from all quarters for failing to show clear leadership and adopting a lofty, even arrogant leadership style, has seen his support fall from 23 percent in May to 17 percent in June, according to the Gallup poll published in the daily Expressen on Sunday.

To add insult to injury, the poll shows that 11 percent of supporters of his own ruling Social Democratic Party would rather see Bildt, a conservative, as prime minister. Bildt was prime minister from 1991 to 1994.

Persson beat Bildt in a 1994 general election but has been forced to rule with a minority government, seeking support from centrists that has cost him the respect of the strong leftist element of his party.

Bildt, on the other hand, has been virtually absent from Swedish politics for the past two years. He was appointed as the U.N.'s representative in Bosnia and has gained major prestige at home for his efforts there.
Bildt is due to make a formal comeback to Swedish politics next month, just over one year before the next general election is due.

The poll was carried out from June 28 to July 2. Some 1,000 Swedes were answering the question; "Who should be prime minister after the next election, Goran Persson, Carl Bildt or another party leader?"
